jobs.description:
Trusted Care. True Compassion.® If that sounds like the kind of team you’d want to be part of, keep reading.

HomeWell Care Services of Middle Tennessee is looking for a Care Manager who loves helping people, stays cool under pressure, and wants to grow with a company that will grow right along with them. We’re a non-medical, in-home care company — which is a fancy way of saying we help older adults and people who need a hand stay safe, happy, and independent in their own homes. Our Care Managers are the glue between our clients, their families, and our caregivers, and it’s one of the most rewarding roles on the team.

In this role you’ll coordinate and supervise the care our clients receive: matching the right caregivers to each client, making sure care plans are followed, checking in with families to keep everyone happy, and jumping in to solve problems before they become problems. If you’re organized, warm, and genuinely love making someone’s day better, you’re going to fit right in here.

We serve clients within a 60-mile radius of Nashville, TN.

What you’ll do

·    Schedule and match caregivers to clients based on needs, personality, and fit.

·    Fill open caregiver shifts as needed to keep every client covered.

·    Supervise client care to ensure caregivers follow the care plan and deliver safe, quality service.

·    Check in regularly with clients and families to make sure they’re happy with their care.

·    Make follow-up calls with new caregivers after first shifts — answer questions, catch issues early.

·    Perform in-home client visits and reassessments as needed.

·    Answer intake calls, schedule assessments, and re-schedule clients when a caregiver calls out.

·    Watch for missed check-ins and make sure caregivers arrive on time.

·    Keep client records current and accurate, and help train caregivers in the home, by phone, or in the office.

·    Serve as a trusted resource for clients and families — education, referrals, and a friendly voice.

The schedule, pay & perks

·    Schedule: Friday through Tuesday (with Wednesday and Thursday off — hello, mid-week weekend!).

·    Pay: $36,000/year salary.

·    Bonus opportunities.

·    Health insurance and supplemental insurance.

·    Paid time off.

·    Opportunity to work from home.

·    A genuinely supportive, positive workplace where your work matters every single day.

·    Lots of room to grow — we love promoting from within, and this role is a launchpad.

A few honest details

·    Some driving is required (you’ll need reliable transportation, a valid license, and current insurance).

·    Some overnight on-call is part of the rotation.

·    Some holiday coverage is required — caring for people doesn’t always take a day off, and we share the load.

What we’re looking for

·    Two years of experience in home care, home health, or a related field.

·    Impeccable follow-up and attention to detail — you track a lot without dropping the ball.

·    Warm, clear communication with clients, families, caregivers, and coworkers.

·    The ability to supervise, assess, and advocate for clients and families.

·    A calm, solution-focused attitude and sound judgment when things get busy.

·    A real passion for helping others live with dignity.

·    Must pass a criminal background check.

If you want a job where you’ll actually see the difference you make — with a team that has your back and a company that wants to see you rise — we’d love to meet you.

You'll work alongside an experienced team, develop your expertise in Plaintiff Personal Injury law, and play a critical role in helping clients receive the care, guidance, and support they need while helping us change lives—one client at a time.

Position Overview

The Plaintiff Personal Injury Intake Case Manager plays a critical role in managing pre-litigation personal injury cases from intake through medical treatment and demand readiness.

This is a high-volume, production-driven position responsible for independently managing an active caseload while serving as the primary point of contact for injured clients throughout the early stages of their case.

The successful candidate will proactively coordinate medical treatment, communicate with insurance adjusters, manage property damage claims, maintain accurate documentation, and ensure each case progresses efficiently toward demand preparation.

This is a full-time onsite position located in Miami Lakes, Florida.

Keep cases progressing toward demand without unnecessary delays.
Coordinate medical treatment and provider follow-up.
Resolve property damage issues efficiently.
Meet departmental KPIs for productivity, responsiveness, and quality.
Maintain complete and accurate case documentation.
Deliver exceptional client service while balancing multiple priorities.

Experience independently managing Plaintiff Personal Injury cases from intake through demand readiness.

Experience communicating directly with insurance adjusters.
Experience coordinating medical treatment and provider follow-up.
Experience managing property damage claims, including total loss, rental coordination, diminished value, and PIP.
Experience requesting and reviewing medical records and bills.
Experience preparing files for demand or attorney review.
Experience managing a high-volume caseload of approximately 300 or more active files.
Experience handling 50 or more inbound and outbound client communications daily.
Experience using Litify (Salesforce) or a comparable legal case management system.
Fluent in English and Spanish.
Ability to work onsite Monday through Friday in Miami Lakes.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience supporting global settlements.
Experience consistently meeting production and quality KPIs.
Experience working in a fast-paced Plaintiff Personal Injury practice.

One Hope United works with children of all ages who are wards of the state due to abuse, neglect or abandonment. These children need a stable, dependable, forever home and a family they can call their own. Safe, well-educated and well-cared-for children become adults who contribute to a more prosperous community. Hundreds of abused, neglected or abandoned children need a stable, nurturing family where they can thrive. One Hope United recruits and trains foster parents and provides myriad supportive services to children and families. Foster parents can light a child’s path toward becoming a successful adult.

Case Managers are responsible for providing direct case management services to children, birth families, foster families and primary caregiver(s) in the home setting, day care, preschool, and/or school to ensure they receive services appropriate to their needs, and continuity of care focused on resolving or preventing the issues of child abuse or neglect. The Case Manager provides assessment, planning, linkage, coordination, monitoring, evaluation and advocacy to the child, family, foster family and primary caregiver. The Case Manager works as a team member with a therapist, foster parents, primary caregiver, guardian ad litem and other appropriate professionals. The Case Manager will develop, strengthen and maintain a direct working relationship with mental health professionals, community agencies and the child’s own support system

Position Responsibilities Include

Arranges visitation schedule structured upon the completed visitation plan with input from the appropriate parties, supervise visitations and document observations as appropriate
Assists in the provision of appropriate information when applicable and accompanies children to appointments, as necessary, to report progress or lack thereof
Assists the primary caregiver(s) and/or foster family in implementing tasks and activities according to the case plan
Attends and participates in professional development training for professional growth as developed by CBC/Pre Service Training, as required by the state of Florida and in accordance with agency policy and procedures
Identifies strengths, limitations, risk factors, and needs, to refer and coordinate the provision of concrete services to the child, primary caregiver, and biological families of children
Serve as a conduit of information between all parties to the case and identified stakeholders, including medical, educational and mental health providers.
Conduct visits with children, parents and/or caregivers that include the on-going assessment of child safety, permanency and well-being.
Develop and implement a plan that meets the needs of the children and the family.
Facilitate placement and delivery of services in collaboration with biological, foster and adoptive families.
Perform case management responsibilities in accordance with state and federal laws, Department of Children and Families Administrative Codes and Operating Procedures, funding source policies and internal policies on child abuse, abandonment, and neglect within required timeframes.
Attend court hearings, prepare and file all court documents within required time frames.
Intervenes and assists OHU/CBC staff in crisis situations
Meet with families in their homes at various hours of the day including evenings, nights and weekends, in potentially high risk neighborhoods.
Attend court hearings, prepare and file all court documents within required time frames.
Other performance related duties per the position job description
